name: How much does it realistically cost to build an ADU in Los Angeles right now?

mainEntity.name: How much does it realistically cost to build an ADU in Los Angeles right now?

acceptedAnswer.text:
In the Los Angeles area, many ground-up ADUs end up in the roughly $275–$450 per square foot range all-in, depending on design, site conditions, and finishes. Garage conversions can be somewhat cheaper per square foot but still add up because kitchens and bathrooms are expensive. 

Sticker shock is normal because an ADU needs almost everything a full house needs—foundation or structural upgrades, kitchen, bathroom, utilities, and permits—just in a smaller package.

Key factors:
- Size and layout complexity (more corners and bathrooms cost more)
- Site access, grading, and distance to utilities
- Level of finishes and custom features
- Soft costs: design, engineering, permits, impact fees

Have your pro give you a range based on concept plans and recent local projects, then build a 10–15% contingency into your budget. That way cost surprises are manageable instead of project-killing.
acceptedAnswer.description: Most Los Angeles ADUs cost roughly $275–$450 per square foot all-in, with garage conversions on the lower end and larger, custom detached units on the higher end. Site access, utility runs, design complexity, and finish level drive the final price more than just square footage.
